# Native aggregates, tagged values and pattern expressions (SIM-007)

The task module runs every positive fixture through the public CLI in both HDL
optimizer modes on legacy, compact/portable and compact/GMP values (GMP when
`LLG_TEST_GMP_ROOT` is set), and after the frontend snapshot and owned Db are
destroyed. Expected outputs are derived by hand from the cited clauses, not
captured from llg.

A one-dimensional fixed unpacked array whose elements are strings, identity
handles or records with string, real or handle members is stored as a fixed
array view of the recursive container runtime: each element is one owned
value, a runtime select reads or writes it in place, and copies are deep
except for handles (SV 7.4, 7.6, 8.4).

| Fixture | Clause and independent oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `native_arrays` | IEEE 1800-2009 §§7.4, 7.4.6, 7.6, 10.4.2, 10.9, 11.4.5, 11.4.11, 13.4. (1) Elements start as empty strings; `$size` is 3. (2) Positional patterns fill in declaration order: `up[1..3]` = a b c, `dn[3..1]` = x y z. (3-6) `always_comb` follows the runtime select `up[k]`: a, then c for k = 3, then C after `up[3] = "C"`, then the empty string for the out-of-range k = 7 (§7.4.6, no warning). (7, 8) Index keys name declared indices and `default` fills the rest: `d two d`; `three ? one`. (9) `'{3{"r"}}` replicates: rrr. (10) The reversing pattern reads every source before writing: rqp. (11) `dn = up` copies by position (dn[3] = up[1]) and stays independent of a later write: `rqp R`. (12) `cp == dn` compares element by element in storage order (r q p both): 1, 0; `cp === up` sees `r` against `R`: 0, 1. (13) `cp[0:1] = dn[2:1]` copies q p: qpp. (14) `cp[k+:2]` with k = 1 takes `up[1:2]` = R q: qRq. (15, 16) A known condition selects one arm: ttt, then `up` = Rqp. (17) An unknown condition keeps equal elements and gives the empty string elsewhere: `[R][][p]`. (18-20) Calls copy the array in and out: `R--p`; `fill` writes z, zz, zzz; a pattern actual is built before the display: `m-n-o`. (21) `rb = ra` copies the records; renaming `rb[0].s` leaves `ra[0]`: `one uno 2 2.5`. (22) `ra == rb` is 0 (one string differs), `!=` 1. (23) `'{default: rec_t'{...}}` fills both records: `9 nine 9 nine`. (24) `swap_pick(ra, 0)` returns `ra[1]` through its swapped local copy: `2 two 2.5`. (25) Nonblocking writes use issue-time values: `up[1]` becomes N1, `up[2]` the old `up[1]` (R), and `rb <= ra` copies record 0 (`1 one`). |
| `handle_records` | §§7.2, 8.4, 13.4, 13.5. Copying a record copies its class handle, so `bump` changes the shared object: `a a+ 11 11 1`. A record element of a fixed array is passed by value and the result stored in another element: `a++ 12 0.25`. An `inout` record formal copies back into an element: `z a+`. Rebinding `b.h` leaves `a.h` at 12; a never-set element handle is null: `12 1 1`. Assigning `a` into `list[0]` shares the object, so writing 99 through the element is seen through `a.h`: 99. |
| `native_tagged` | §§7.3.2, 11.9, 12.6, 12.6.1, 12.6.2. A tagged union with string, real, record, class-handle and packed members keeps the tag and each member separately. (1) `tagged I 5` reads 5. (2) `x.S` is appended to while S is active and `y = x` copies it (`str!`); `x` then holds F = 2.5. (3) `y matches tagged S .s` binds `str!`; (4) `x` holds F, so the S test fails. (5) `tagged F .r &&& r > 2.0` binds 2.5 and prints 5.0. (6) The record member is assigned by a pattern and updated in place: `rec 8`; (7) `tagged Rec .*` matches. (8) A handle member shares its object: 30 written through `x.H` is read through `b`. (9) `tagged B 8'h5a` matches exactly; (10) the binding `.k` with filter `k[0] == 0` prints `5a`. (11) In plain `case`, `?` digits are literal Z bits, so `8'b0101????` does not match `5a`: default; (12) `casez` treats them as wildcards: matches. (13) `tagged None` selects the void item. (14) A binding in a case item feeds its `&&&` filter: `case`. |
| `native_tagged_inactive` | §§7.3.2, 11.9. Every inactive access reports `access to inactive tagged-union member` with its source location and run-time failure (exit 1; the reports go to stderr and the `$display` lines to stdout): (1) the never-assigned union has no active member, so `x.S` reports and reads the empty string; (2) with I active, `x.S` and `x.F` report and read `""` and 0.0; (3) the write `x.S = "lost"` reports and stores nothing, then `x.I = 9` succeeds; (4) with S active the write to I reports and `x.S` still reads `kept`. |
| `witness_tagged_native`, `witness_string_binding`, `witness_string_array_pattern`, `witness_record_slice`, `witness_string_array_return` | Adopted FND-002 witnesses (ledger L-F02-09-01/L-F05-08-03 `tagged_native`, L-F05-08-02 `native_pattern_match`, L-F05-05-02 `native_array_pattern`, and the SIM-003 child items `record_slice` and `string_array_return`); each expected line is the witness's `Expected:` header; the copies end with a quiet `$finish(0)`. |
| `native_member_select` | §§7.4.6, 13.5. Run-time indices into member arrays of a module record and of a record formal. (1) `k = 1` reads `b`, `a[2] = 7`, `r[1] = 1.5`. (2) Writes through `k` set `s[1] = B`, `a[1] = 5`. (3) `k = 9` is out of range: reads give `""`, 0 and 0.0; (4) the writes store nothing, so the record is unchanged (`aBc`, `0 5 7 0`). (5) An X index (`logic` variable) reads the defaults. (6) The formal copy of `n` is edited at index 1 (`xwz/w`); index 2 reads `z`; index -1 reads `""`; (7) `n` itself is unchanged. (8) Editing the copy of `m` at index 2 gives `aBw/w`. (9) Packed member selects: `p = 5a`, `p[3:0] = c` gives `5c`, `p[7] = 1` gives `dc`; `p[7:4]` is `d` and `p[1]` is 0. |
| `member_select_limit`, `bad_member_select_limit` | Boundary of the 64-element run-time selection bound: 64 elements are accepted (`s[3] = x`, `s[63] = y`, untouched `s[2]` is empty), 65 are rejected at code generation with the bound in the message. |
| `record_element_equality` | §§7.2, 11.4.5. Whole record elements of queues, dynamic and associative arrays compare member-wise against each other and module records. (1) `q[0]` and `p[0]` hold equal members: 1; `q[1]` differs from `p[0]`: 0; `!=` gives 0; `q[1] == m`: 1. (2) `m == q[1]` and `d[1] == q[1]` (both copies of `m`): 1; the default `d[0]` differs from `q[0]`: 0. (3) `a["x"]` is a copy of `m`: equal to `d[1]`, not to `d[0]`. (4) `k = 7` is past the queue end, so `q[7]` reads the default: equal to `d[0]`, unequal to `p[0]`. (5) After `q[0].s = "A"` the string member differs: 0; the member reads `A`: 1. (6) `4'b10x1` members: `===` matches the X exactly (1, `!==` 0) while `==` is unknown (`x`). |
